brief_summary: Five-panel numbered process strip for the H2 'Liquid spill response'. Panel 1: a board edge with its cable pulled away, gap between plug and port. Panel 2: a tilted board with keycaps coming loose. Panel 3: a folded cloth pressed onto a puddle blob with inward absorb arrows. Panel 4: a tipped dropper bottle releasing droplets onto a small switch rectangle. Panel 5: an upright board surrounded by short radiating dash marks suggesting air-drying. Each panel matches one of the five bolded steps in the article body verbatim — power down, flip and pull keycaps, blot, isopropyl flush, full dry-out before reassembly.
data_sources: apps/web/src/content/articles/keyboard-cleaning-maintenance-guide.mdx — 'Power down and disconnect immediately. Unplug the cable, or hold a wireless board's power switch off.'

apps/web/src/content/articles/keyboard-cleaning-maintenance-guide.mdx — 'Flip the board and pull keycaps. Tipping it lets standing liquid drain away from the switches instead of pooling, and removing keycaps... exposes the stems and stabilizer wells'
apps/web/src/content/articles/keyboard-cleaning-maintenance-guide.mdx — 'Blot, don't wipe. A cloth pressed straight down onto standing liquid pulls it up'

apps/web/src/content/articles/keyboard-cleaning-maintenance-guide.mdx — 'Isopropyl flush for sticky residue. ... A swab or syringe with 90%+ isopropyl alcohol, worked into the switch stems and stabilizer wells, cuts through it.'

apps/web/src/content/articles/keyboard-cleaning-maintenance-guide.mdx — 'Full dry-out before reassembly. Measured in days, not hours... A fan on the open board, or a sealed container with desiccant, speeds the process without adding heat.'
